items.title: Home Depot vs. Lowe’s: One Housing Recovery Play Stands Out
items.summary: Both Home Depot and Lowe's are fighting the same frozen housing market, but their Q2 earnings reveal a widening gap between two very different strategies. One company is gaining ground while the other is quietly retreating.

items.title: Tariffs Hurt Williams-Sonoma More Than the Housing Market
items.summary: Williams-Sonoma  stock dropped on Wednesday even though the home specialty retailer delivered a beat-and-raise quarter in tough times for housing.  The stock is up 25% this year, but down 11% from its all-time closing high of $251.78 on Aug. 7, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  While other retailers are logging tariff refunds, Williams-Sonoma is feeling a sting.

items.title: Home Depot Stock's Upside Case Now Runs Through A Business It Bought
items.summary: The distribution arm inside Home Depot has gone from dragging comparable sales down to comping above the company average, and that shift is the clearest upside lever left while housing stays frozen.

items.title: Williams-Sonoma Stock Dips Despite Q2 Earnings and Revenue Beat
items.summary: WSM beats fiscal Q2 earnings and revenue estimates and raises its 2026 outlook, but shares dip as tariffs pressure adjusted margins.

items.summary: Pro and online growth offset DIY weakness amid housing market headwinds.

items.title: How big box retailers are using tariff refunds
items.summary: Walmart is investing its $2.9 billion return into price cuts, while Target plans for additional reimbursements and Home Depot and Lowe’s offset higher costs.
